interactions: Donepezil + Amlodipine: no significant pharmacokinetic interaction; amlodipine does not slow the heart rate.
Donepezil + Aspirin 81 mg: no pharmacokinetic interaction; cholinesterase inhibitors increase gastric acid secretion, which adds modestly to the gastrointestinal bleeding risk of aspirin.
Donepezil + Calcium carbonate or vitamin D3: no significant interaction.
warnings: Cholinesterase inhibitors can cause bradycardia, heart block and syncope; check pulse before starting and after dose increases (heart rate 72 bpm at this visit) and ask about dizziness or falls.
Nausea, diarrhoea, anorexia, vivid dreams and insomnia are common at initiation; start at 5 mg and increase to 10 mg after 4 to 6 weeks if tolerated; morning dosing if sleep is disturbed.
No dose adjustment is needed for mild reduction in kidney function.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic multi-domain impairment on MMSE and MoCA with no cue benefit, informant-confirmed decline over a year, and loss of instrumental independence (medicines, finances, appointments, stove safety)
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive assessment with informant history, a per-domain profile and an explicit account of daily function
action_criteria.rationale: Her husband's account of medicines, finances and stove safety decides the stage, and his report of fluctuations has to be weighed against Lewy body disease [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Severe verbal memory impairment with poor recognition, impaired visual memory, mild naming and processing speed deficits and impaired set-shifting
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the profile and set a baseline
action_criteria.rationale: Formal memory testing shows whether the deficit is storage-type (Alzheimer) or retrieval-type with attentional and visuoperceptual predominance (Lewy body or vascular) [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No reversible cause; LDL 148 mg/dL and total cholesterol 228 mg/dL elevated in a hypertensive patient not taking a statin
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid, B12, folate, syphilis and HIV must be excluded, and vascular risk (lipids, renal function) measured in a hypertensive patient [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Medial temporal atrophy (MTA 2, left slightly greater than right) with Fazekas grade 2 white matter hyperintensities and a chronic left putaminal lacune
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with a dementia protocol to assess medial temporal atrophy and cerebrovascular disease and exclude a mass
action_criteria.rationale: MRI shows the medial temporal atrophy of Alzheimer disease and measures the small vessel disease that contributes to her decline [NIA_AA_2011] [STRIVE_2013].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and here it decides whether Alzheimer pathology rather than small vessel or Lewy body disease drives the decline [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in APP, PSEN1 or PSEN2
action_criteria.label: Offer an early-onset Alzheimer gene panel only after pre-test genetic counselling; do not use APOE genotype as a diagnostic test
action_criteria.rationale: Onset at 61 makes APP, PSEN1 and PSEN2 testing an option to discuss, but her mother's dementia began in her 70s, so a pathogenic variant is unlikely and the result would inform family counselling rather than the diagnosis [ACMG_NSGC_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No clinically significant interaction with amlodipine, aspirin, calcium or vitamin D; modest additive gastrointestinal risk with aspirin; pulse 72 permits a start at 5 mg
action_criteria.label: Check interactions before starting donepezil
action_criteria.rationale: Before a cholinesterase inhibitor her amlodipine, aspirin and supplements should be reviewed and the pulse checked, given her positional dizziness [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the decline to depression: the depressive episode was 8 years ago and resolved, and the memory deficit is objective and progressive

Do not prescribe an antipsychotic for the hypnagogic images; they are not distressing, and antipsychotics carry increased mortality in dementia and severe sensitivity reactions if Lewy body pathology is present [NICE_NG97]
Do not start memantine at the mild dementia stage; it is indicated for moderate or severe Alzheimer dementia [NICE_NG97]
required_recommendations: Obtain collateral history from an informant who knows the patient well
Disclose the diagnosis of mild Alzheimer dementia with a cerebrovascular contribution to her and her husband, and plan durable power of attorney, advance directives and support for her husband

Address safety now: supervised or automatic shut-off cooking, medicines in a blister pack given by her husband, her husband taking over finances and appointments, and a formal driving assessment if she drives

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].
Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines [NICE_NG97].

Manage vascular risk: start a statin for LDL 148 mg/dL given hypertension and a lacunar infarct with Fazekas 2 small vessel disease, and keep blood pressure at target (138/82 mmHg today on amlodipine)
Measure lying and standing blood pressure for her positional lightheadedness and adjust amlodipine if orthostatic hypotension is found
Review at follow-up for features of Lewy body disease (well-formed hallucinations when awake, dream enactment, parkinsonism, marked fluctuation) and investigate further if they appear

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG does not contribute to the dementia work-up; she has no syncope, palpitations or QT-prolonging medicine, and her positional lightheadedness calls for lying and standing blood pressure, not an ECG
Echocardiography is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardioembolic indication in this presentation
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; no arrhythmia, syncope, or palpitations described
Head CT adds little when MRI is available; MRI is the preferred structural modality for dementia workup

accepted: Early-onset Alzheimer disease (mild dementia, amnestic) with cerebrovascular contribution

differential.key_features: Raised by mild daytime fluctuations, hypnagogic images and positional lightheadedness, with a maternal uncle with Parkinson disease. Against it: images only on falling asleep and recognized as unreal (not core visual hallucinations), no dream enactment, no parkinsonism, a storage-type memory deficit with MTA 2 atrophy, and an Alzheimer CSF profile. Lewy co-pathology cannot be excluded; reassess if core features emerge
No early personality change, disinhibition or progressive aphasia; amnestic profile with medial temporal atrophy and Alzheimer biomarkers

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment as the sole cause
differential.key_features: Fazekas 2 white matter disease and a putaminal lacune are a real contributor, but the gradual amnestic course with poor recognition, MTA 2 atrophy and an Alzheimer CSF profile show Alzheimer disease as the primary cause
Remote resolved episode; current low mood is reactive (GDS 6/15), and recall is not helped by cues or recognition

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or sleep-related cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: TSH, free T4, B12, folate, RPR and HIV normal; no symptom of sleep apnoea

key_clinical_evidence: Loss of instrumental independence (medicines only with reminders, help with finances and appointments, repeated stove incidents) stages the syndrome as mild dementia, not mild cognitive impairment [NIA_AA_2011]

Fazekas 2 white matter disease and a lacune are a contributing cerebrovascular copathology, but they do not explain an amnestic storage-type deficit with medial temporal atrophy and an Alzheimer CSF profile [STRIVE_2013]
Mild fluctuations and hypnagogic images alone do not meet criteria for dementia with Lewy bodies; follow the patient for core features, and avoid antipsychotics
One conclusive amyloid biomarker test (CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau, or amyloid PET) is enough [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET]

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Chen Wei is a 62-year-old right-handed retired schoolteacher who presents to the neurology outpatient clinic accompanied by her husband for evaluation of progressive memory difficulties over the past 12 months. Her husband first noticed changes approximately one year ago when she began misplacing everyday items such as her keys and reading glasses with increasing frequency. Over the subsequent months, she started forgetting recent conversations, sometimes asking the same questions multiple times within an hour. Approximately six months ago, she had an episode of becoming disoriented while walking in their neighborhood of 20 years, briefly unable to find her way home from the local market, which alarmed both patient and family. She has had several instances of leaving the stove on after cooking and forgetting to take her medications unless reminded. Her husband reports she has become less engaged in social activities and recently withdrew from her weekly mahjong group, citing difficulty keeping track of the tiles and game strategy. She has also had intermittent episodes of dizziness described as lightheadedness, particularly with position changes, which she attributes to her blood pressure medication. Of note, she occasionally reports vivid, brief dream-like images when falling asleep, describing scenes of people she does not recognize appearing in her bedroom doorway, though she recognizes these as not real. Her husband notes that her alertness and engagement seem to fluctuate throughout the day, with periods of being quite sharp alternating with periods of seeming 'foggy' or staring into space, though these fluctuations have been mild. She denies any falls, gait difficulties, tremor, hallucinations during full wakefulness, or loss of consciousness. She has not experienced any sudden neurological deficits, headaches, seizures, or changes in personality. She reports her mood has been somewhat low given her frustration with the memory problems, though she denies hopelessness, anhedonia, or suicidal ideation. She continues to perform basic activities of daily living independently but requires increasing assistance with managing finances and scheduling appointments.
